title: PARTNER CONTENT: When Faster Supercomputers Aren’t Enough
gist: Sponsored SC26 profile of Argonne's Ravi Madduri: rewriting the SAIGE genetics code for GPUs (SAIGE-GPU) made Million Veteran Program analysis feasible (2,068 traits, 635,969 veterans, 13,672 regions) and federated learning via APPFL is the path for cross-institution medical compute.

insights.claim: A genome-wide association study on the Million Veteran Program cohort would not finish on Summit's CPUs because the per-group matrix no longer fit in memory as the cohort grew, so the problem was code design, not raw speed.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Software architecture can block science that faster hardware alone does not fix, a case for GPU-porting investment.
insights.locator: What The Math Was Unable To Solve

insights.claim: The analysis spent nearly all its time multiplying very large grids of numbers, the operation GPUs exist to do; rewriting that part as SAIGE-GPU made an analysis requiring roughly 481,000 CPU-core hours tractable.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Matrix-heavy scientific workloads migrate to GPUs, widening accelerator demand beyond AI.
insights.locator: So, the team, led on this effort by Argonne's Alex Rodriguez

insights.claim: Madduri says the same computational architecture accelerating AI discovery is also foundational for population genomics.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: AI-driven GPU buildouts also serve scientific HPC.
insights.quote: is also foundational for population genomics
insights.locator: What The Math Was Unable To Solve

insights.claim: Tasks that took 14 days when the Science paper was written now take less than a couple of hours, enabling larger cohorts and more statistical rigor.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude runtime cuts let researchers repeat studies at larger scale.
insights.quote: Things that took 14 days when we wrote the Science paper now take less than a couple of hours

insights.claim: The study covered 2,068 traits across 635,969 veterans and flagged 13,672 genome regions linked to one or more conditions.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Scale of the biobank analysis shows demand for large compute in precision medicine.

insights.claim: About 1,600 of the regions surfaced only because nearly a third of participants were not of European ancestry; they appear only when separate ancestry-group analyses are combined.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Diverse cohorts reveal otherwise invisible targets, relevant to drug-discovery data strategies.

insights.claim: Madduri stresses the results are preclinical, a statistical map of where to look, and turning any region into a treatment takes years of downstream work.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: No near-term therapeutic revenue implied; discovery phase only.

insights.claim: Medical data cannot be shared as freely as cosmology data, so federated learning moves the model to data held at each institution and combines only the learned adjustments.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Privacy-preserving training is the route for multi-institution medical AI.
insights.quote: Federated learning allows you to train models without moving data around

insights.claim: APPFL, the Argonne Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning framework, submits training jobs via Globus Compute, which presents one interface across facility schedulers; the harder problem is permission since each job must run under the collaborator's own institutional credentials and project allocation.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Access control and authorization, not ML, are the bottleneck for cross-site computing.

insights.claim: A site with unique data makes the shared federated model more robust for everyone.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Data uniqueness is the incentive for participation in federations.
insights.locator: If one site has data that are unique to it

insights.claim: Cross-institution computing is still largely manual, with Madduri's team talking to NERSC, Argonne and Oak Ridge separately, and he hopes the American Science Cloud under DOE's Genesis Mission will automate it via APIs.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: A DOE federated compute layer could drive demand for national lab infrastructure.
insights.quote: It is a lot of human in the loop

insights.claim: Madduri says agentic approaches are the next frontier for his group.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: AI agents are spreading to scientific workflow orchestration.
insights.quote: The agentic approaches are the next frontier for us

insights.claim: This piece is partner content promoting SC26 (Chicago, November 15-20, 2026), so it is promotional framing of the research story.
insights.speaker: Charity Plata
insights.so_what: Treat as sponsored; research claims come from one interviewee.
